claims.statement: On bls12-381-g1-ecdlp-plain (input T=[x]P0, x uniform in [0,r), no auxiliary powers), the algorithm in this package recovers and verifies x by [x]G=T with probability at least 0.3739, measured as a one-sided Clopper-Pearson bound on the shipped escape-armed walk (DP spacing 2^-5, 16 walkers, visits/sqrt(N) asserted within 1e-3 of the ledger budget 1.0096963), using at most 2^126.266 native-equivalent work units at C=2000. The measured production-shape row is 0.373911 (evidence/walk-census.json:arms[-1].cp95 minus the ledger debits); the model decomposition at 2^20 walkers and DP spacing 2^-60 is 0.3995 = 1-exp(-S(S-1)(w-1)/(2Nw)) at S = 1.0096963*sqrt(N), reported as a model row with its walker factor and DP window stated analytically, not measured. Absorption on the repaired predecessor-dependent process is measured at two sizes: 16,384 starts per size, P(absorbed) = 1.0 at both, period_2 = 0 (the two-step repair removes exactly the 2-cycles), 3-cycle share of the residual 0.0263 -> 0.0007 over a 4.0x class increase, with a re-pin mutation control that moves the counts by 0.7810. Restart cost is regenerated by script from itemised 383-instruction products (476.644 ref per 256-bit scalar action, 1,485.1600 ref per fresh start), ledger.py consumes that JSON, and scripts/selfaudit.py enforces that every cited file exists, every cited field resolves, and a planted wrong path is caught. The deterministic work cap is charged as an expenditure bound only; no lossless-cap claim is made.

title: Plain G1 v20n: absorption evidence shipped with cycle-length split (2/3/>=4) and re-pin control, restart chain repriced by script into the ledger, citation path audit with planted control - 126.266
